findings.message: github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk v0.7.3: no Protocol 30 support; releases before v0.8.0 lack the CAP-88 ledger close-value XDR arms and the CAP-84 W strkey, so they cannot decode ledger headers closed after the upgrade
findings.remediation: Upgrade to github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk v0.8.0 or later (it requires Go 1.25.0 or newer).

findings.message: decodes xdr.LedgerCloseMeta with github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk v0.7.3, whose XDR lacks the CAP-88 StellarValue arms; every ledger closed after the Protocol 30 upgrade will fail to decode
findings.evidence: func Decode(b64 string) (xdr.LedgerCloseMeta, error) {; SDK from indexer/go.mod:5: go.mod requires github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk v0.7.3
findings.remediation: Upgrade to github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk v0.8.0 or later (it requires Go 1.25.0 or newer).

findings.message: MustLcValueSignature reads only the STELLAR_VALUE_SIGNED arm and panics on ledgers closed after the Protocol 30 upgrade, which use STELLAR_VALUE_SIGNED_MS (CAP-88)
findings.remediation: Use StellarValueExt.LedgerCloseValueSignature() (go-stellar-sdk v0.8.0+), which reads the signature from every arm.

findings.message: divides by the difference of two whole-second close times; after CAP-88 consecutive ledgers can close within the same second, so the divisor can be 0
findings.remediation: Guard the divisor against 0, or use the millisecond close time (closeTimeMs in the STELLAR_VALUE_SIGNED_MS arm), which strictly increases.

findings.message: SDK address checks accept G, M, C but not W: muxed-contract addresses (CAP-84) are rejected where muxed and contract addresses are both allowed
findings.remediation: If this value can be a payment or transfer destination, accept W too: StrKey.isValidMuxedContract (@stellar/stellar-sdk 17.3.0+) or strkey.IsValidMuxedContractAddress (go-stellar-sdk v0.8.0+). W addresses are 69 characters long, like M addresses.

findings.message: @stellar/stellar-sdk 16.3.1: no Protocol 30 support; this version lacks the CAP-88 ledger close-value XDR arms and the CAP-84 W strkey; only 16.4.x and 17.3.0+ decode Protocol 30 ledgers
decodes ledgers from rpc getLedgers() with @stellar/stellar-sdk 16.3.1, whose XDR lacks the CAP-88 StellarValue arms; every ledger closed after the Protocol 30 upgrade will fail to decode
findings.evidence: const { ledgers } = await server.getLedgers({ startLedger });; SDK from web/package.json:5: package.json dependencies declares "@stellar/stellar-sdk": "16.3.1"
findings.remediation: Upgrade to @stellar/stellar-sdk 17.3.0 or later (16.4.x also decodes Protocol 30 ledgers).

findings.message: address regex accepts G, M, C but not W: muxed-contract addresses (CAP-84) are rejected where muxed and contract addresses are both allowed
findings.remediation: If this value can be a payment or transfer destination, accept W too: StrKey.isValidMuxedContract (@stellar/stellar-sdk 17.3.0+) or strkey.IsValidMuxedContractAddress (go-stellar-sdk v0.8.0+). W addresses are 69 characters long, like M addresses.

limitations: Static, offline analysis only: scanned code is never executed, and no network or RPC calls are made.
A finding is an indication to review, not proof of runtime breakage; no findings is not proof of Protocol 30 compatibility.
Stellar's November 3, 2026 (Testnet) and November 23, 2026 (Mainnet) dates are upgrade votes, not guaranteed activation dates.
Ignored directories, symlinks that are not followed, and files over the size limit are not inspected; see the skipped list.
